arxiv-1902-06458.title: Temporal Wheeler’s delayed-Choice Experiment based on Cold Atomic Quantum Memory
arxiv-1902-06458.creator: Ming-Xin Dong, Dong-Sheng Ding, Yi-Chen Yu, Ying-Hao Ye, Wei-Hang Zhang, En-Ze Li, Lei Zeng, Kan Zhang, Da-Chuang Li, Guang-Can Guo, Bao-Sen Shi
arxiv-1902-06458.description: Abstract Nowadays the most intriguing features of wave-particle complementarity of single photon is exemplified by the famous Wheeler’s delayed choice experiment in linear optics, nuclear magnetic resonance and integrated photonic device systems. Studying the wave-particle behavior in light and matter interaction at single photon level is challenging and interesting, which gives how single photons complement in light and matter interaction.

arxiv-2105-02500.title: Universality classes of the Anderson transition in three-dimensional symmetry classes AIII, BDI, C, D and CI
arxiv-2105-02500.creator: Tong Wang, Tomi Ohtsuki, Ryuichi Shindou
arxiv-2105-02500.description: Abstract We clarify universal critical properties of delocalization-localization transitions in three-dimensional (3D) unitary and orthogonal classes with particle-hole and/or chiral symmetries (classes AIII, BDI, D, C and CI). We first introduce tight-binding models on cubic lattice that belong to these five nonstandard symmetry classes respectively.

arxiv-2105-14561.title: Rotationally Symmetric Extremal Kähler Metrics on ℂ n \mathbb{C}^{n} and ℂ 2 ∖ { 0 } \mathbb{C}^{2}\setminus\{0\}
arxiv-2105-14561.creator: Selin Taşkent
arxiv-2105-14561.description: Abstract In this paper, we study rotationally symmetric extremal Kähler metrics on ℂ n \mathbb{C}^{n} ( n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 ) and ℂ 2 \ { 0 } \mathbb{C}^{2}\backslash\{0\} . We present a classification of such metrics based on the zeros of the polynomial appearing in Calabi’s Extremal Equation.

arxiv-2201-11752.title: Gas dynamics in dwarf galaxies as testbeds for dark matter and galaxy evolution
arxiv-2201-11752.creator: Federico Lelli
arxiv-2201-11752.description: Abstract Dwarf galaxies are ideal laboratories to test dark matter models and alternative theories because their dynamical mass (from observed kinematics) largely outweighs their baryonic mass (from gas and stars). In most star-forming dwarfs, cold atomic gas forms regularly rotating disks extending beyond the stellar component, thus probing the gravitational potential out to the outermost regions.

arxiv-2302-00756.title: Quantum Decay of an Optical Soliton
arxiv-2302-00756.creator: Stuart Ward 1,2, Rouzbeh Allahverdi 1, Arash Mafi 1,2
arxiv-2302-00756.description: Abstract Optical solitons are known to be classically stable objects which are robust to perturbations. In this work, we show that due to quantum mechanical effects, an optical soliton that is initially in a classical soliton coherent state will shed photons into the continuum and hence decay.

arxiv-2305-02902.title: Biased versus unbiased numerical methods for stochastic simulations
arxiv-2305-02902.creator: Javier Aguilar, José J. Ramasco, Raúl Toral
arxiv-2305-02902.description: Abstract Abstract Approximate numerical methods are one of the most used strategies to extract information from many-interacting-agents systems. In particular, numerical approximations are of extended use to deal with epidemic, ecological and biological models, since unbiased methods like the Gillespie algorithm can become unpractical due to high CPU time usage required.

arxiv-2310-14903.title: A New Approach to Calculate Coronal Electron Density: Simplified van de Hulst’s Method Volume: 0
arxiv-2310-14903.creator: H. Çakmak 1 ​ \cc {}^{1\cc} \orcid 0000-0002-1959-6049 \affsep 1 İstanbul University, Faculty of Science, Department of Astronomy and Space Sciences, 34116, Beyazıt, İstanbul, Türkiye
arxiv-2310-14903.description: Abstract Determining the electron density is a challenging task in solar corona studies, as it requires certain assumptions to be made, such as symmetric, homogeneous and radial distribution, thermal equilibrium, etc. In such studies, the observed K K corona brightness is based on the coronal electron density.

arxiv-2402-13113.title: When Only Time Will Tell: Interpreting How Transformers Process Local Ambiguities Through the Lens of Restart-Incrementality
arxiv-2402-13113.creator: Brielen Madureira Patrick Kahardipraja David Schlangen
arxiv-2402-13113.description: Abstract Incremental models that process sentences one token at a time will sometimes encounter points where more than one interpretation is possible. Causal models are forced to output one interpretation and continue, whereas models that can revise may edit their previous output as the ambiguity is resolved.

arxiv-2404-04447.title: Quasinormal modes of a nonsingular spherically symmetric black hole effective model with holonomy corrections
arxiv-2404-04447.creator: Douglas M. Gingrich
arxiv-2404-04447.description: Abstract We calculate the quasinormal modes of a nonsingular spherically symmetric black hole effective model with holonomy corrections. The model is based on quantum corrections inspired by loop quantum gravity. It is covariant and results in a spacetime that is regular everywhere with a parameter-dependent black bounce.

arxiv-2411-00306.description: Abstract We measure the time-integrated C ​ P C\!P asymmetry in D 0 → K S 0 ​ K S 0 D^{0}\rightarrow K^{0}_{\rm\scriptscriptstyle S}K^{0}_{\rm\scriptscriptstyle S} decays reconstructed in e + ​ e − → c ​ c ¯ e^{+}e^{-}\rightarrow c\overline{c} events collected by the Belle and Belle II experiments.

arxiv-2501-01505.title: Reinforcement Learning for Respondent-Driven Sampling
arxiv-2501-01505.creator: Justin Weltz, Angela Yoon, Yichi Zhang, Alexander Volfovsky, Eric Laber
arxiv-2501-01505.description: Abstract Respondent-driven sampling (RDS) is widely used to study hidden or hard-to-reach populations by incentivizing study participants to recruit their social connections. The success and efficiency of RDS can depend critically on the nature of the incentives, including their number, value, call to action, etc.

arxiv-2502-20697.title: Stochastic lensing of stars by ultralight dark matter halos
arxiv-2502-20697.creator: Andrew Eberhardt, Elisa G. M. Ferreira, Wentao Luo, Shurui Lin, Yin Li
arxiv-2502-20697.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrew Eberhardt, Elisa G. M. Ferreira, Wentao Luo, Shurui Lin, Yin Li. Ultralight dark matter is an interesting dark matter candidate describing the lightest end of the mass parameter space. This model produces an oscillating granular pattern in halo densities. These fluctuations have the potential to produce a time-varying density along the line of sight creating a small lensing signal for any stars observed through a dark matter halo which oscillates on the de Broglie timescale.

arxiv-2503-05828.title: Market-based Architectures in RL and Beyond Conference: Proc. of the 24th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2025); May 19 – 23, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA bs034 CCS: Theory of computation Algorithmic game theory and mechanism design CCS: Computing methodol
arxiv-2503-05828.creator: Abhimanyu Pallavi Sudhir, Long Tran-Thanh
arxiv-2503-05828.description: Abstract . Market-based agents refer to reinforcement learning agents which determine their actions based on an internal market of sub-agents. We introduce a new type of market-based algorithm where the state itself is factored into several axes called “goods”, which allows for greater specialization and parallelism than existing market-based RL algorithms.

arxiv-2508-07591.title: Weighted eigenvalues of Dirac operators: complete continuity and comparison Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject classification: 35P05, 35F05, 47A75, 49R05
arxiv-2508-07591.creator: Zixuan Qiu, Ruijun Wu
arxiv-2508-07591.description: Abstract . We give a min-max characterization of all of the weighted Dirac eigenvalues, and show that the weighted eigenvalues and eigenspaces of Dirac operators are continuous with respect to weak L p L^{p} convergence of the inverse weights, for any p > n p>n .

arxiv-2509-10213.title: Dynamic Vulnerability Patching for Heterogeneous Embedded Systems Using Stack Frame Reconstruction CCS: Computer systems organization Firmware CCS: Security and privacy Vulnerability management
arxiv-2509-10213.creator: Ming Zhou, Xupu Hu, Zhihao Wang, Haining Wang, Hui Wen, Limin Sun, Peng Zhang
arxiv-2509-10213.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ming Zhou, Xupu Hu, Zhihao Wang, Haining Wang, Hui Wen, Limin Sun, Peng Zhang. Existing dynamic vulnerability patching techniques are not well-suited for embedded devices, especially mission-critical ones such as medical equipment, as they have limited computational power and memory but uninterrupted service requirements. Those devices often lack sufficient idle memory for dynamic patching, and the diverse architectures of embedded systems further complicate the creation of patch triggers that are compatible across various system kernels and hardware platforms.

arxiv-2601-07113.creator: Natham Aguirre

pmc-11406563.creator: Opeyemi Oladapo-Shittu, Sara E. Cosgrove, Clare Rock, Yea-Jen Hsu, Eili Klein, Anthony D. Harris, Carlos Mejia Chew, Heather Saunders, Patrick R. Ching, Avi Gadala, Stephanie Mayoryk, Lisa Pineles, Lisa L. Maragakis, Alejandra B. Salinas, Taylor Helsel, Sara C. Keller, for the Centers for Disease Co
pmc-11406563.description: ne-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) are likely underestimated because only those that occur more than 72 hours after admission to an acute care hospital are routinely reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN).

pmc-11597078.title: Integrin Targeting and Beyond: Enhancing Cancer Treatment with Dual-Targeting RGD (Arginine–Glycine–Aspartate) Strategies
pmc-11597078.creator: Bojana Bogdanović, Daniel Fagret, Catherine Ghezzi, Christopher Montemagno, Guillermina Ferro-Flores
pmc-11597078.description: Integrins, an important superfamily of cell adhesion receptors, play an essential role in cancer progression, metastasis, and angiogenesis, establishing them as prime targets for both diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Despite their significant potential, integrin-targeted therapies have faced substantial challenges in clinical trials, including variable efficacy and unmet high expectations.

pmc-11888653.title: Eggshell Derived Nanohydroxyapatite as a Bone Graft for Intrabony Defects was Evaluated Using (CBCT) - A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-11888653.creator: Vishnuvarthan Ganapathy, Anitha Balaji, T S Sampath Kumar, Mohanasatheesh Shanmugam
pmc-11888653.description: Aim:The study aims to assess the effectiveness of eggshell-derived nanohydroxyapatite (EnHA) as a bone graft material for treating intrabony defects, using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) for evaluation.Materials and Methods:Ten patients were divided into two groups: Group 1: individuals with 2-wall defects, Group 2: those with 3-wall defects.

pmc-12583124.title: Sensor-based evaluation of intermittent fasting regimes: a machine learning and statistical approach
pmc-12583124.creator: Nico Steckhan, Tanja Manlik, Tillmann Int-Veen, Beeke Peters, Christina Laetitia Pappe, Daniela A. Koppold, Bert Arnrich, Andreas Michalsen, Henrik Dommisch, Peter Schwarz, Olga Pivovarova-Ramich
pmc-12583124.description: The primary aim was to develop and assess the performance and applicability of different models utilizing sensor data to determine dietary adherence, specifically within the context of intermittent fasting. Our approach utilized time-series data from two completed human trials, which included continuous glucose monitoring, acceleration data, and food diaries, and a synthetic data set.

pmc-12619834.title: From neglected to notoriety: a review of Mpox clinical features, virology, epidemiology, treatment and prevention strategies
pmc-12619834.creator: Clément Viguier, Pierre Delobel, François-Xavier Lescure, Simon Bessis, Jean-Michel Mansuy, Guillaume Martin-Blondel
pmc-12619834.description: PurposeThis narrative review aims to provide an overview of current knowledge on mpox, emphasizing updated epidemiology and recent advances in treatment and prevention strategies, in light of the latest outbreaks.MethodsWe searched PubMed and Google Scholar for publications on ‘Mpox’ and ‘Monkeypox’ up to June 5, 2025.

pmc-12849640.title: Prostate cancer risk and antioxidant biomarkers: the age-dependent reversal of bilirubin’s role
pmc-12849640.creator: Jong Won Shin, Jae Woong Sull, Nguyen Thien Minh, Sun Ha Jee
pmc-12849640.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundProstate cancer incidence increases markedly after midlife, coinciding with age-related hormonal decline and alterations in antioxidant defense mechanisms. This study investigated age-specific associations between endogenous antioxidant markers (total bilirubin, albumin, and uric acid) and prostate cancer risk.MethodsData were derived from the Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II (KCPS-II), and a total of 83,371 men were included after excluding individuals with a history of cancer or missing key variables at baseline.

pmc-12992139.title: Elevated Peripheral White Blood Cell Count and Lower Urinary Tract Symptom Risk: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study of Chinese Men
pmc-12992139.creator: Zheng Lu, Jiange Zhang, Zhenyuan Yu, Jiawen Zhao, Zhifu Zhang, Shengzhu Huang, Min Qin, Chunlei Wu, Zengnan Mo, Ming Liao
pmc-12992139.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the association between peripheral white blood cell (WBC) count and lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in a male population.Study Design and SettingA population-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among males aged 18–88 years in Fangchenggang, Guangxi, China, from July to November 2011. Using multistage cluster sampling, 4,694 participants were enrolled. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed the WBC-LUTS association.

pmc-13220350.title: Stress first aid for the harm reduction workforce: pilot test results of an occupational stress intervention
pmc-13220350.creator: Anmol Desai, Juliette Rau, Jake Samora, Katie A McCormick, Haresh Rochani, Patrick Chang, Richard J Westphal, Patricia J Watson, Justin K Benzer, Kasey R Claborn, Suzannah K Creech
pmc-13220350.description: BackgroundHarm reduction workers (HRWs), while fighting the overdose crisis, are exposed to lifetime occupational stress and trauma, which in turn are associated with the long-term work and social functioning of this key sector. There is a critical gap in research on the occupational health of HRWs.

pmc-13223658.title: Qualitative study of barriers and facilitators to Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) on the Caribbean island of Montserrat
pmc-13223658.creator: Bill Berners-Lee, Nadine Duberry, Dorothea Hazel-Blake, Christian Mallen, Thomas Shepherd, Anna S Tirion, Dale Weston, Sharra Greenaway-Duberry, Riinu Pae
pmc-13223658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionHypertension is the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, with high prevalence in the Eastern Caribbean. Dietary modification is central to prevention and management, with the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet supported by strong clinical evidence. DASH promotes increased consumption of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts, seeds and pulses while limiting salt, sugar, high-fat meats and dairy, and refined carbohydrates. Although promoted in primary care in Montserrat, adherence may be limited by structural, social and cultural barriers.

pmc-13233307.title: A paradigm shift in the treatment of patients with polycythemia vera. The initial early use of recombinant interferon-alpha
pmc-13233307.creator: Richard T Silver, Hans Carl Hasselbalch
pmc-13233307.description: During the past 35 years, single-arm studies documented the efficacy and safety of recombinant interferon alpha (rIFNα) for treating polycythemia vera (PV). In some patients, 2-5 years of disease-modifying treatment resulted in symptom relief, regression of splenomegaly, normalization of abnormal blood counts and marrow morphology, and sustained JAK2V617F molecular remission.

pmc-13314325.title: Effects of the methanolic extract of Tradescantia spathacea on nitro-oxidative and chemokine responses in peritoneal macrophages from BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice
pmc-13314325.creator: Diana L. Chávez-Aviña, Ángeles G. Lugo-Díaz, Kibsaim Franco-Villanueva, Víctor I. Lozano-Vielmas, Gustavo Hernández-Vidal, Raymundo A. Pérez-Hernández, Adolfo Soto-Dominguez, Uziel Castillo-Velázquez
pmc-13314325.description: Background:During innate immunity, peritoneal macrophages (PMs) orchestrate early nitro-oxidative and chemokine responses, and their polarization is influenced by mouse strain-dependent metabolic programs. Tradescantia spathacea is a medicinal plant with reported anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; however, its effects on macrophage nitro-oxidative and chemokine responses remain unclear.Aim:To investigate the effects of a methanolic extract of T. spathacea (MET.

pmc-13356679.title: Virtual reality for opioid reduction in postoperative cardiac and thoracic surgery: A randomized controlled trial protocol
pmc-13356679.creator: David Duarte de Araujo, Suely Pereira Zeferino, Filomena Regina Barbosa Gomes Galas
pmc-13356679.description: This protocol describes a randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the efficacy of Virtual Reality (VR) as a non-pharmacological intervention for pain management in the immediate postoperative period of cardiac and thoracic surgeries. Postoperative pain in these major procedures is often intense and historically managed with high doses of opioids, which are associated with significant side effects and potential dependence.

pmc-13499055.title: Gene deletions differentially affect surface-associated biofilms and staphylococcal abscess communities
pmc-13499055.creator: Darine D'Adam, Marco Chittò, Livia S Kiener, T Fintan Moriarty, Elian MA Kuhn
pmc-13499055.description: Staphylococcus aureus is a major human pathogen that causes persistent infections characterised by the formation of aggregates such as surface-attached biofilm and staphylococcal abscess communities (SACs). Both consist of dense bacterial populations associated with self-produced matrices that impair immune cell and antibiotic access.

pmc-13586812.title: A case of suspected Sjögren's disease–associated pleuritis in a very elderly patient
pmc-13586812.creator: Riko Sato, Takefumi Nikaido, Takahiro Kumanaka, Hiroaki Kume
pmc-13586812.description: A 90-year-old woman presented with an antibiotic-resistant fever and right-sided pleural effusion. Pleural fluid analysis revealed exudative effusion without identifiable pathogens. Sjögren's disease (SjD) was diagnosed based on anti-SS-A/SS-B antibody positivity and labial salivary gland biopsy findings. Pleural effusion was suspected to be associated with SjD, although a definitive causal relationship could not be established.

pmc-13595162.title: HOMEBRED: A unified CRISPR platform for field-ready shadowing of infectious agents and oncogenic mutations
pmc-13595162.creator: Adnan Asadbeigi, Hassan Fazilaty, Mojtaba Saffari, Reza Shirkoohi, Mohammad Hossein Modarressi, Abdoalreza Salehi, Mohammad Reza Bakhtiarizadeh
pmc-13595162.description: SummaryEmerging infectious diseases and late-stage cancers demand rapid, sensitive, and deployable diagnostics. Here, we present HOMEBRED (highly sensitive & specific omnipresent multipurpose endonuclease based reliable detection), a CRISPR-based platform capable of detecting human and animal pathogens (viral/bacterial, RNA/DNA) alongside oncogenic transcripts.
